**Starts** once #60 and #57 are merged.

## Why

The weather worker writes each stay's weather and what to wear, from a forecast or from seasonal averages (technical spec 6.3, functional spec 8). It's the last worker.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 1 (agent types), 4.2 (weather and clothing), 5.2, 5.3 (the weather worker's worker brief), 6.3, and 6.5 (how a worker is started, its result, and the hooks).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), sections 2.1 (`set_stay_weather` and `read_worker_brief_facts`), 2.5 (`look_up_stay_weather`), 2.6 (`report_result`), and 3.
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), sections 8 and 9.6.

## Open questions

- ~~**How does the weather worker tell that an activity is far from the stay's town?** `look_up_stay_weather` takes either the stay's town or an attraction far from it, such as Tuolumne Meadows on a Yosemite stay (tool design 2.5). `read_worker_brief_facts` gives each activity's place with its short line (technical spec 7.2), and the short line's town is the worker's best clue. But the short line has no town when Google's address has none, as for "Delicate Arch Trail, Utah, USA" (`Place.town` in `src/domain/place.ts`). Park attractions, the ones most likely to be far away, often have no town. Raised on 2026-10-28, from a review note on #201.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** code adds the distance, and the worker judges. Each activity line from `read_worker_brief_facts` adds how far its place is from the stay's town, as the crow flies, such as "about 18 miles from Yosemite Valley". Both places' coordinates are stored, and `milesBetween()` in `src/tools/search-result-lines.ts` works it out. An activity with no place yet gets no distance. The weather worker's instructions say to look up an activity's own weather when its weather could differ from the town's: by height, such as Tuolumne Meadows at about 8,600 feet against about 4,000 in Yosemite Valley, or by a local climate, such as the coast against inland. The distance tells the worker where the place is when its name and address don't. The model knows the height and local climate of well-known places. Two choices were left out. A distance limit in code would be wrong both ways, since height and local climate matter more than distance, and it's a fiddly rule. Looking up every activity makes many calls that mostly repeat the town's weather, and takes away the judgment worth watching in a trace. This leans on the model's judgment, local climates most of all. Whether that gives good results is to be seen in traces, and tuned only if it's a problem.
- ~~**What does `set_stay_weather` call its stay ID input?** #198's hooks record each `mcp__trip__set_stay_weather` call, and read the stay it saved from the input's `stayId`, the name `add_lodging_candidates` uses (`src/agent/worker-calls.ts`). The result lists the stays the weather worker read but saved nothing for, so a different name would list every stay as missing. Proposed: name it `stayId`, as the other tools do. If it's named otherwise, change the hook's schema in the same PR. Raised on 2026-10-28, while #198 was being built.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** `stayId`. It was never really open: #198's hook already reads that name, and every other tool that takes a stay uses it. It's now a point under "Do".
- ~~**How does the `weather` server get into the session?** `createWeatherServer()` exists (`src/tools/weather-server.ts`), but the query's `mcpServers` doesn't hold it yet, so no agent can be sent `look_up_stay_weather`. #198 left it out, since no agent used it yet. Proposed: add it to the query's `mcpServers`, and `mcp__weather` to `allowedTools`, with its access in `CoordinatorGiven` and `coordinatorAccessFor()`, as the other servers are. Technical spec 6.5 says every server is in the session, and the definitions pick who gets each tool. Raised on 2026-10-28, while #198 was being built.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** as proposed. Technical spec 6.5 already says so, and only the weather worker's definition lists `look_up_stay_weather` (tool design section 3), so the coordinator doesn't get it. It's now a point under "Do".

## Do

- Add `set_stay_weather`, the weather worker, and its instructions. Its instructions include #60's text on problems and questions word for word: `PROBLEMS_AND_QUESTIONS` in `src/agent/worker-instructions.ts` (technical spec 6.4).
- Name `set_stay_weather`'s stay input `stayId`, as the other stay tools do. #198's hook in `src/agent/worker-calls.ts` reads the saved stay by that name.
- Add the `weather` server to the query's `mcpServers` and `mcp__weather` to `allowedTools`, and build its access in `CoordinatorGiven` and `coordinatorAccessFor()`, as the other servers are. Only the weather worker's definition lists `look_up_stay_weather` (tool design section 3).
- Add each activity's distance from the stay's town to its line in `read_worker_brief_facts`, and to the tool's description, and write it into tool design 2.1 and 2.5 (the settled question above). Drop the comment in `src/tools/activity-lines.ts` that says #64 settles how the worker tells.
- Give the weather worker a definition as technical spec 6.5 says, with the type `weather-worker` and its tools from tool design section 3, and add `weather-worker` to the coordinator's `Agent(...)` entry. Its worker brief holds only stay IDs, and it calls `read_worker_brief_facts` first, as the other workers do.
- Write the weather worker's worker brief as the "Fill:" heading (`WORKER_BRIEF_HEADING.fill` in `src/agent/worker-instructions.ts`), with one stay ID per line, and no other heading. Add a line to the "Worker briefs" section of `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` that says so, since that section says every worker brief has every heading. The weather worker's instructions name only that heading. Write it into technical spec 5.3. The other headings are always there so a stay researcher or leg scout never wonders whether one was left out, and the weather worker uses none of them. Decided on 2026-10-28 in chat.
- Add a model setting and an effort setting for the weather worker, like the stay researcher's, and pass both into its definition. Each agent has its own, so one agent's model or effort can change and be evaluated alone. Decided on 2026-10-28 in chat, in place of #208. Both start as the stay researcher's do: `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `medium`. Its text is short, but it leans on the model knowing the height and local climate of places, such as Tuolumne Meadows against Yosemite Valley, which a smaller model is weaker at. It can be tried on a smaller model later, with an evaluation. Add the two rows to technical spec section 10, as "Weather worker model" and "Weather worker effort". Decided on 2026-10-28 in chat.
- Add the coordinator's rules for when to run and rerun it. One is in the session-start bullet of technical spec 5.2: when the full read at the start of a session shows a stay whose seasonal averages could now be a forecast, offer to rerun the weather worker for it. #54 left this out of the instructions, since the worker didn't exist yet.
- Show each stay's weather and clothing text in the itinerary view, with its label, an out-of-date mark, and its credit: the Open-Meteo credit on seasonal averages (Open-Meteo design section 4), and "Includes data from Google Maps" on a forecast. Put each at the bottom of that stay's weather block. Google's [Weather API policies](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/weather/policies) give that text for "entirely new content" made from the data, and the worker's text is its own reading of the forecast. The credit goes "near the top or bottom of the content, and within the same visual container", always visible, and never changed. Write the rule into Google design section 3, with the link. #62 adds a Google Maps credit to the option cards, so whichever merges second reuses the first one's. Decided on 2026-10-28 in chat.

## Done when

- The Moab trip (domain model, section 5.2) gets weather and clothing text for both stays, and Torrey's covers freezing-night stargazing.
- Moving the trip one day later doesn't mark seasonal averages out of date.
- Adding a stay marks it out of date.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

But the short line has no town when Google's address has none, as for "Delicate Arch Trail, Utah, USA" (`Place.town` in `src/domain/place.ts`). Park attractions, the ones most likely to be far away, often have no town. Raised on 2026-10-28, from a review note on #201.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** code adds the distance, and the worker judges. Each activity line from `read_worker_brief_facts` adds how far its place is from the stay's town, as the crow flies, such as "about 18 miles from Yosemite Valley". If it's named otherwise, change the hook's schema in the same PR. Raised on 2026-10-28, while #198 was being built.

Proposed: add it to the query's `mcpServers`, and `mcp__weather` to `allowedTools`, with its access in `CoordinatorGiven` and `coordinatorAccessFor()`, as the other servers are. Technical spec 6.5 says every server is in the session, and the definitions pick who gets each tool. Raised on 2026-10-28, while #198 was being built.
